source_boundary: Original authored teaching scenarios aligned to supplied course; not copied assessment questions.

scenarios.title: Peroxide Decomposition
scenarios.context: A sealed virtual record identifies hydrogen peroxide before the change and water plus oxygen afterward. The mixture warms without external heating.
strong_evidence: Substance identity changed from hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen
scenarios.response: Isolate the record and label the case for review; do not perform unknown mixing.
scenarios.transfer_skill: New substance identity is stronger evidence than bubbles alone.

scenarios.title: Cooling Solution
scenarios.context: A solid dissolves and the container cools. A later recovery test identifies the same solid.
scenarios.alternate: Not enough information before the identity comparison is opened
scenarios.transfer_skill: Cooling and dissolving alone do not prove chemical change.

scenarios.title: Corroding Tool
scenarios.context: A clean iron tool is left in moist air and develops a reddish-brown coating with new properties.
strong_evidence: New iron–oxygen product with different appearance and properties
supporting: Mass can increase as oxygen becomes part of the product
scenarios.response: Use a barrier coating to reduce contact with oxygen and moisture.
scenarios.transfer_skill: Matter from the surroundings can become part of a product.

scenarios.title: Antacid Record
scenarios.context: A calcium-carbonate antacid reacts with stomach acid in a supplied virtual record.
scenarios.accepted: Acid–carbonate reaction within the unit's neutralization context
strong_evidence: Carbon dioxide, water and a calcium salt are identified
scenarios.response: Use only the supplied record; no dose or treatment advice.
scenarios.transfer_skill: Classify from reactants/products, not bubbles alone.

scenarios.title: Methane Combustion
scenarios.context: Methane reacts with oxygen in a controlled virtual burner record.
strong_evidence: Carbon dioxide and water are identified as products
supporting: Thermal and light energy are released
scenarios.response: Identify carbon dioxide as the product connected to the environmental issue studied in Unit A.
scenarios.transfer_skill: Connect reaction evidence, category and consequence.

scenarios.title: Boiling Water
scenarios.context: Liquid water forms bubbles; the vapour is collected and condenses back to water.
scenarios.transfer_skill: Bubbles do not automatically mean a chemical reaction.
